title: Schooling and family; farm life in Iowa
description: The interviewee explains that she did not continue school because she stayed home with her mother as the last daughter, while her father traveled to places like Ohio building grain elevators. She mentions her younger brothers Roy and Eric and that she never held outside jobs such as clerking or teaching. The family moved among farms in Iowa, selling and renting land before building a home.

title: Hobbies; box suppers; magic lantern shows
description: She names reading as her lifelong hobby and mentions sewing club work with friends. She describes community box suppers where decorated boxes of food were auctioned for several dollars, and recalls traveling magic lantern shows projected on a curtain, including a performance of Uncle Tom's Cabin.

title: Parties; picnics; Fourth of July; county fairs
description: She remembers birthday parties and summer picnics, including a July 15th gathering where families spread dinners on the ground. She describes old-fashioned Fourth of July celebrations with speeches held in the park near town, and county fairs where women entered apples and other produce.

title: Childhood then and now; churches; railroad towns
description: She contrasts her childhood with her children's, recalling walking to a country schoolhouse every two miles and attending evangelistic meetings held there. She notes that little towns were built along the Northern Pacific railroad, which placed a town about every seven miles.

title: Courtship; meeting her husband; clothing and buggies
description: She recalls courting with buggy rides and Sunday drives, and describes the white dresses, button shoes, hats, and umbrellas she wore as a girl. She explains that she met her husband while visiting relatives near Fonda, Iowa, enjoyed going to dances, and married after about a year and a half together, afterward coming to Spokane.

title: Marriage; cattle ranching; homesteading and wells
description: She explains that she married into a family of prominent ranchers who raised and sold cattle and horses. She describes her expectation of independence after marriage giving way to hard work proving up land with no well, and recalls men drilling through solid rock, finally reaching water after months of effort.
